name: bnx2_set_link
prose: Updates bp->link_up from the PHY and reprograms the MAC; bp must point to an initialised bnx2 adapter and the caller must serialise access to it (bnx2.c:1552-1633). Returns 0 on every return in the function (1559, 1563, 1632); it has no error return. If bp->loopback is MAC_LOOPBACK or PHY_LOOPBACK it sets bp->link_up = 1 and returns at once, without reading the PHY, without calling bnx2_report_link and without calling bnx2_set_mac_link. Otherwise, if bp->phy_flags has BNX2_PHY_FLAG_REMOTE_PHY_CAP it returns 0 without changing any field. Otherwise it saves the old bp->link_up, reads the BMSR register twice (bnx2_enable_bmsr1 / bnx2_disable_bmsr1 around the reads), and for a SERDES phy on a 5706 chip it first calls bnx2_5706s_force_link_dn(bp, 0) and clears BNX2_PHY_FLAG_FORCED_DOWN if that flag was set, then recomputes BMSR_LSTATUS from BNX2_EMAC_STATUS_LINK and the AN-debug shadow register (NOSYNC bit). If BMSR_LSTATUS is then set it sets bp->link_up = 1, runs the SERDES linkup routine for the 5706/5708/5709 chip (or bnx2_copper_linkup for a non-SERDES phy; a SERDES phy on another chip gets no chip-specific linkup call) and calls bnx2_resolve_flow_ctrl. If it is clear it calls bnx2_disable_forced_2g5 when the phy is SERDES with AUTONEG_SPEED set, and, whatever the phy type, if BNX2_PHY_FLAG_PARALLEL_DETECT is set it sets BMCR_ANENABLE in the BMCR and clears that flag; it then sets bp->link_up = 0. On the non-early path it calls bnx2_report_link only if bp->link_up differs from the value at entry, and then calls bnx2_set_mac_link before returning 0.
note: Second reviewer's 'skips BMSR and set_mac_link' is right and the old prose already said so; the 'contradicts exactly when differs' claim is mixed: the loopback path does skip report_link, but the 'exactly' applied only to the non-early path. Reworded to say so. Parallel-detect branch is not conditional on SERDES (1614).

name: bnx2_start_xmit
prose: Transmit entry point: queues one skb on the TX ring chosen by skb_get_queue_mapping(skb) (bnx2.c:6573-6743); the caller owns skb and dev. Returns NETDEV_TX_BUSY (6597) only when bnx2_tx_avail() is less than skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags + 1 on entry: it then stops the queue (netif_tx_stop_queue), logs 'BUG! Tx ring full when queue awake!' and does not touch or free the skb. Otherwise it builds the flag word (TX_BD_FLAGS_TCP_UDP_CKSUM for CHECKSUM_PARTIAL, VLAN tag when present, software-LSO flags and header-length/offset encoding when gso_size is non-zero, using tcp_optlen and ip_hdr(skb)->ihl for non-IPv6 GSO) and dma-maps the linear part with dma_map_single. If that mapping fails it frees the skb with dev_kfree_skb_any and returns NETDEV_TX_OK (6651) with the ring untouched. It then fills a START descriptor and one descriptor per page fragment, mapping each with skb_frag_dma_map; if a fragment mapping fails it goes to dma_error, which resets tx_buf->skb at the original producer slot, unmaps the head and the earlier fragments, frees the skb and returns NETDEV_TX_OK (6742) without advancing txr->tx_prod. On success it sets TX_BD_FLAGS_END on the last descriptor, does wmb(), netdev_tx_sent_queue, advances tx_prod and tx_prod_bseq by skb->len, writes the two mailbox registers, and returns NETDEV_TX_OK (6718); after that, if bnx2_tx_avail() <= MAX_SKB_FRAGS it stops the queue, does smp_mb() and wakes it again if avail > bp->tx_wake_thresh. So NETDEV_TX_OK is returned for sent skbs and for the two skb-dropped-on-mapping-error cases; NETDEV_TX_BUSY only in the full-ring case.
note: Reviewer's claim (stops when avail <= MAX_SKB_FRAGS, not 'fewer than') is mixed: the entry check is avail < nr_frags+1 (6592) and busy, while the <= MAX_SKB_FRAGS test (6705) is a separate post-send stop. Both are described now. Slice cut head: real function 6573-6743.

name: bnx2x_ets_e3b0_config
prose: Programs the E3B0 ETS (enhanced transmission selection) hardware for params->port from ets_params (bnx2x_link.c:1128-1229). params, vars and ets_params must be valid; vars is used (bnx2x_ets_get_min_w_val_nig(vars), 1136) to pick the NIG minimum weight from the link speed. It validates its inputs itself and returns -EINVAL when the chip is not E3B0 (1148), when ets_params->num_of_cos exceeds the per-port maximum (DCBX_E3B0_MAX_NUM_COS_PORT0 or _PORT1, 1154), when bnx2x_ets_e3b0_get_total_bw fails (1166), or when a COS entry's state is neither bnx2x_cos_state_bw nor bnx2x_cos_state_strict (1200). It writes the NIG and PBF credit upper bounds before the per-COS loop, so an error in or after the loop leaves those and any earlier COS register writes in place (no rollback). In the loop a bw-state COS sets its bit in a bandwidth bitmap and calls bnx2x_ets_e3b0_set_cos_bw (programming NIG and PBF weights and credits), a strict-state COS sets its bit in a strict bitmap and records its priority via bnx2x_ets_e3b0_sp_pri_to_cos_set; a non-zero status from either is returned as-is (1205). After the loop it writes the strict-priority register (bnx2x_ets_e3b0_sp_set_pri_cli_reg) and the client mapping (bnx2x_ets_e3b0_cli_map), returning their non-zero status as-is, and otherwise returns 0 (1228).
note: All three earlier reviewer claims check out against the code: partial register commits before an error (1172-1205), the E3B0/num_of_cos checks return -EINVAL (1145-1155), and vars is passed to bnx2x_ets_get_min_w_val_nig (1136). Reviewers right 3/3.

name: bnx2x_init_one
prose: PCI probe for a bnx2x device (bnx2x_main.c:13824-14026). pdev is the PCI device and ent its pci_device_id entry; the early returns below do not undo any PCI enabling or region claims. On a kdump kernel it first sleeps until 5 s after boot. Early returns before a netdev exists: the negative value from set_max_cos_est(ent->driver_data) (13856), -EINVAL if the RSS queue count (non-default status blocks minus the CNIC one) is below 1 (13869), and -ENOMEM if alloc_etherdev_mqs fails (13882). It then initialises bp (flags, igu_sb_cnt, igu_base_addr, msg_enable, cnic_support, cnic_probe) and calls pci_set_drvdata. If bnx2x_init_dev returns a negative value it calls only free_netdev(dev) and returns that value (13900-13901): it does not iounmap, release regions or disable the device there. If bnx2x_init_bp fails it goes to init_one_exit; the later failures go to init_one_freemem: VF doorbell/PCI allocation (bnx2x_vf_pci_alloc), PF doorbell BAR too small for BNX2X_L2_MAX_CID*(1<<BNX2X_DB_SHIFT) (-ENOMEM) or ioremap failure / NULL bp->doorbells (-ENOMEM), bnx2x_vfpf_acquire for a VF, bnx2x_iov_init_one, bnx2x_set_int_mode, and register_netdev. init_one_freemem calls bnx2x_free_mem_bp and falls into init_one_exit, which iounmaps bp->regview if set, iounmaps bp->doorbells only for a PF with a non-NULL mapping, calls free_netdev, calls pci_release_regions only when pdev->enable_cnt == 1, calls pci_disable_device, and returns the saved rc. On success it also sets qm_cid_count and the number of queues, sets NO_FCOE_FLAG on E1x chips, adds the FCoE SAN address under rtnl_lock when FCoE is not disabled, may set the OS driver state to DISABLED (unless MF SD storage-only personality), and returns 0 (14006).
note: Reviewer (bnx2x_init_dev failure only does free_netdev) is right: 13898-13902. Slice cut the head; real function starts 13824.

name: bnx2x_int_mem_test
prose: Self-test of the internal memories using loopback packets (bnx2x_main.c:6690-6833); bp must be an initialised bnx2x device whose register accessors work, and the function sleeps (usleep_range/msleep). It disables the parser neighbour inputs, zeroes the PRS CFC-search credit, sends one loopback packet (bnx2x_lb_pckt) and polls NIG_REG_STAT2_BRB_OCTET through bnx2x_read_dmae until it equals 0x10, up to 1000*factor tries (factor 120 on FPGA, 200 on emulation, else 1); on timeout it logs and returns -1 (6730) with the neighbour inputs still disabled. It then polls PRS_REG_NUM_OF_PACKETS for 1 and returns -2 on timeout (6745) without having reset anything. Next it resets BRB and PRS through the MISC reset registers and reruns bnx2x_init_block for BLOCK_BRB1 and BLOCK_PRS, repeats the input disable, sends 10 packets and polls the NIG octet counter for 0xb0, returning -3 on timeout (6786). The two checks that PRS_REG_NUM_OF_PACKETS equals 2 and 3 only log an error and do not change the return value. It then reads the NIG EOP loopback FIFO 11 times and returns -4 if NIG_REG_INGRESS_EOP_LB_EMPTY is not 1 (6810). Otherwise it resets and reinitialises BRB and PRS again (the NIG block is not reinitialised, despite the comment), writes PRS_REG_NIC_MODE=1 when CNIC_SUPPORT(bp) is false, re-enables the four parser neighbour inputs and returns 0 (6832). So the reset/re-init of BRB and PRS and the re-enable happen only on the 0 return, apart from the first BRB/PRS reset that precedes the -3 and -4 returns.
note: Reviewers: round-2 claim (early -1/-2/-4 returns skip the reset) right for -1/-2 (-4 comes after the first reset but before the second); round-15 claim that NIG is not re-initialised is right (6818-6819 only BRB1 and PRS); first claim (PRS val!=2/3 only log) right. 3/3 right.

name: bnx2x_init_hw_common
prose: Common-phase hardware initialisation of a bnx2x chip, run by the first function loaded on a path (bnx2x_main.c:7052-7491; the packet name bnx2x_init_common is not the real name, and the slice shows only the middle part). bp must be an initialised adapter; the function sleeps. It takes HW_LOCK_RESOURCE_RESET only around the chip reset sequence (bnx2x_reset_common and the MISC reset-set writes) and releases it before the first return that can fail, so no error return holds that lock. It then initialises the MISC, PXP, PXP2 blocks; on non-E1x chips it disables the PF master enable for the other functions on the path through bnx2x_pretend_func/bnx2x_pf_disable, applies the E2 timers-ILT workaround (clearing the whole ILT via a dummy TM client), and initialises ATC (waiting up to a bounded number of 200 ms polls for ATC_REG_ATC_INIT_DONE); it initialises the DMAE, TCM, UCM, CCM, XCM, QM (plus TM when CNIC_SUPPORT), DORQ, BRB1, PRS, the four SDMs and SEMs, UPB, XPB, PBF, SRC, CDU, CFC, HC, IGU, MISC_AEU and NIG blocks with the PHASE_COMMON tables, with several chip-dependent register writes (AFEX header registers, VFC memory resets, search keys written only when CNIC_SUPPORT) in between, and sets bp->dmae_ready = 1 early (it is not cleared on a later error). Returns -EBUSY (after logging) in these cases only: PXP2_REG_RQ_CFG_DONE or PXP2_REG_RD_INIT_DONE not 1 (7125, 7130); ATC_REG_ATC_INIT_DONE not 1 on a non-E1x chip (7249); CFC_REG_LL_INIT_DONE, AC_INIT_DONE or CAM_INIT_DONE not 1 after reg_poll (7446, 7451, 7456); on E1 only, when the NIG BRB octet counter is zero and bnx2x_int_mem_test returns non-zero (7469). On E1 it can therefore have reset the chip and initialised many blocks before returning -EBUSY. Otherwise, after enabling attentions/parity, setting up fan-failure detection, calling bnx2x__common_init_phy on E1x when the bootcode (MCP) is present (it only logs when MCP is missing) and writing netproc_fw_ver to SHMEM2 when that field exists, it returns 0 (7490).
note: Slice contained only the middle of the function and the packet name is wrong; real function is bnx2x_init_hw_common at 7052-7491, read in full except the long E2 comment block. Old reviewers only said 'name not in slice' (mechanical, right).

name: bnx2x_func_chk_transition
prose: Checks whether the function-object command params->cmd is legal in the current state o->state and, if so, records the successor in o->next_state (bnx2x_sp.c:5812-5908; the packet name bnx2x_func_state_transition does not exist and the slice cut the head, so this is the real function holding the shown switch). If RAMROD_DRV_CLR_ONLY is set in params->ramrod_flags it first sets o->pending = 0 and o->next_state = BNX2X_F_STATE_MAX. If o->pending is then non-zero it returns -EBUSY without changing o->next_state (beyond the clear above). Otherwise a switch on o->state accepts: from RESET only HW_INIT (-> INITIALIZED); from INITIALIZED START (-> STARTED) or HW_RESET (-> RESET); from STARTED STOP (-> INITIALIZED), TX_STOP (-> TX_STOPPED), and AFEX_UPDATE, AFEX_VIFLISTS, SWITCH_UPDATE or SET_TIMESYNC (each staying STARTED, but only while BNX2X_F_CMD_STOP is not pending in o->pending); from TX_STOPPED SWITCH_UPDATE or SET_TIMESYNC (staying TX_STOPPED, again only while STOP is not pending) and TX_START (-> STARTED). An unknown state logs 'Unknown state'. If a successor was found it stores it in o->next_state and returns 0; any other command/state combination logs and returns -EINVAL, leaving o->next_state as it was.
note: Packet function name was wrong and it was marked dropped; fixed under the real name per rule 6. Previous prose not reviewed against this (only mechanical 'name not in slice', which was right). Note -EBUSY return the old prose lacked.

name: bnx2x_vfpf_acquire
prose: VF-side acquire of resources from the PF over the VF-PF mailbox (bnx2x_vfpf.c:223-393); tx_count and rx_count are the requested queue counts and bp->vf2pf_mbox is assumed initialised. It prepares an ACQUIRE TLV (with a physical-port-id TLV, EXT_BULLETIN and VLAN_FILTER capabilities and a list-end TLV). It returns -EAGAIN if bnx2x_get_vf_id fails (237), or if the PF replies with a status other than PFVF_STATUS_SUCCESS and either that status is not PFVF_STATUS_NO_RESOURCE or the attempt count has reached VF_ACQUIRE_THRESH (334); in the latter case it logs an old-hypervisor message when the FP-HSI TLV says unsupported. If bnx2x_send_msg2pf fails it returns that call's own error code unchanged (rc at 282-283), not a fixed -EAGAIN. On NO_RESOURCE with attempts left it lowers each requested resource (txqs, rxqs, sbs, mac/vlan/mc filters) to the minimum of the request and the PF's recommended value, clears the response buffer and resends. After success it copies the physical port id into bp->phys_port_id and sets HAS_PHYS_PORT_ID if the PF returned that TLV. If the response has no FP_HSI_SUPPORT TLV and ETH_FP_HSI_VERSION is newer than ETH_FP_HSI_VER_2, it calls bnx2x_vfpf_finalize and bnx2x_vfpf_release, and returns -EINVAL. Otherwise it fills bp from bp->acquire_resp (chip_id, db_size, IGU info, mf_mode, flags, igu_sb_cnt, igu_base_sb, vlan_credit, fw_ver, and the MAC address if valid) and returns 0. Every path reaches the out label, which calls bnx2x_vfpf_finalize(bp, &req->first_tlv) once more (so the -EINVAL path above finalises twice).
note: Reviewer (returns that call's negative error code, not -EAGAIN, on send_msg2pf failure) is right: 277-283. Slice cut the head; real function 223-393.

name: bnxt_init_one
prose: PCI probe for a Broadcom bnxt device (bnxt.c:16880-17156; the packet name bnxt_probe is not the real name). It returns -ENODEV if pdev is a PCI bridge or has no MSI-X capability, and in a kdump kernel returns the failure value of bnxt_kdump_reset if that fails; it returns -ENOMEM if alloc_etherdev_mqs fails. Those returns happen before the netdev exists. After that it fills the private bnxt (board index, flags, devlink port for a PF) and every later failure sets rc and jumps to a cleanup label, finally returning rc after free_netdev. Failures that go to init_err_pci_clean: bnxt_alloc_hwrm_resources, bnxt_fw_init_one_p1, bnxt_alloc_rss_indir_tbl, bnxt_fw_init_one_p2, bnxt_map_db_bar, bnxt_init_mac_addr (rc then forced to -EADDRNOTAVAIL), bnxt_probe_phy, bnxt_set_dflt_rings (rc forced to -ENOMEM unless it is -ENODEV on a VF), bnxt_init_int_mode, and failure to create the PF workqueue (-ENOMEM). A bnxt_init_board failure goes directly to init_err_free (free_netdev only). A bnxt_dl_register failure goes to init_err_dl, and a register_netdev failure to init_err_cleanup. A bnxt_init_tc failure is only logged, and a failure of bnxt_pcie_dsn_get has its rc overwritten by the next call, so neither aborts the probe. init_err_cleanup uninitialises the aux devices, frees the aux device id and unregisters devlink, then falls through to init_err_dl (shutdown TC, clear int mode) and init_err_pci_clean (HWRM unregister, PTP clear, free ptp_cfg, HWRM resources, hwmon, ethtool, fw_health, bnxt_cleanup_pci, ctx and crash-dump memory, rss_indir_tbl). The aux-device init and auxdev id allocation (17055-17057) happen before several of the jumps to init_err_pci_clean (rings, int mode, workqueue) and before bnxt_dl_register fails to init_err_dl, and those labels do not call bnxt_aux_devices_uninit or bnxt_auxdev_id_free. On success (17128) it has registered the netdev, created devlink fw reporters, added the aux devices, printed the device info, called pci_save_state and returns 0.
note: Reviewer (init_err_pci_clean omits aux device/id cleanup) is right: aux init at 17055-17057, cleanup only in init_err_cleanup 17129-17132. Slice cut the head; real function 16880-17156.

name: __bnxt_get_coredump
prose: Builds the firmware coredump (bnxt_coredump.c:403-527). bp is the device; if buf is NULL only the length is computed, otherwise buf must have room and *dump_len must hold the caller's buffer size on entry (buf_len). *dump_len is overwritten: it first becomes the size of the first segment (segment header plus the hwrm_ver_get response, which is copied into buf when buf is non-NULL). For dump_type BNXT_DUMP_DRIVER it adds the length from bnxt_get_ctx_coredump and goes to the err tail with rc 0. Otherwise it lists the firmware segments (bnxt_hwrm_dbg_coredump_list; on failure it logs and goes to err with that rc), adds a header per segment, and for each segment (a) returns -ENOBUFS via err if buf is non-NULL and the header would not fit within BNXT_COREDUMP_BUF_LEN(buf_len), (b) calls bnxt_hwrm_dbg_coredump_initiate; if that fails it logs and skips retrieval (its rc stays in rc and is recorded in the segment header), (c) otherwise calls bnxt_hwrm_dbg_coredump_retrieve; -ENOBUFS goes to err, any other error is logged and kept in rc, (d) writes the segment header (and advances offset by header plus seg_len) when buf is non-NULL and adds seg_len to *dump_len. A non-fatal initiate/retrieve error is overwritten by the next segment's rc, so the returned rc reflects only the last segment's status (or -ENOBUFS); a failure on the last segment is therefore returned. The err tail writes the coredump record when buf is non-NULL (with the rc), frees coredump.data, and if rc is 0 adds sizeof(struct bnxt_coredump_record) to *dump_len and, when buf_len is non-zero, sets *dump_len = buf_len, i.e. the caller's buffer size, not the bytes written. On -ENOBUFS it logs 'Firmware returned large coredump buffer'. It returns rc.
note: Round-15 reviewer (final *dump_len is bytes written, not buffer size) is WRONG: 521-522 set *dump_len = buf_len when rc==0 and buf non-NULL. Round-1 (non-fatal errors can be overwritten) right; round-2 (error on last segment is returned) right; original reviewer (contract omits dump_len) not applicable now (no contract). Slice cut the head; real function 403-527.

name: hwrm_req_dma_slice
prose: Hands out a DMA-able buffer of 'size' bytes for an HWRM request (bnxt_hwrm.c:777-819; the packet name bnxt_hwrm_dma_alloc is not the real name and the slice starts mid-function). req is the request buffer returned by the HWRM request allocator, whose context is looked up with __hwrm_ctx(bp, req); *dma_handle receives the DMA address. If there is no context it returns NULL (no other effect). Otherwise it computes an aligned offset inside the request buffer area below the space already allocated (BNXT_HWRM_DMA_SIZE minus ctx->allocated, minus size, aligned down to BNXT_HWRM_DMA_ALIGN); if the resulting address lies above the request length (ctx->req_len) and below the already-allocated area, it records ctx->allocated, sets *dma_handle = ctx->dma_handle + offset and returns that address inside the request buffer (no new mapping). If that does not fit and a separate slice already exists (ctx->slice_addr non-NULL) it logs 'HWRM refusing to reallocate DMA slice' with the request type, calls dump_stack() and returns NULL. Otherwise it calls dma_alloc_coherent(size, ctx->gfp); on failure it returns NULL, on success it stores ctx->slice_addr/slice_size/slice_handle, leaves the address in the new mapping and returns it (*dma_handle set by dma_alloc_coherent). At most one separately mapped slice is kept per context.
note: Real function name is hwrm_req_dma_slice (found by reading the file above the slice, 777-819); the previous 'name not in slice' mechanical rejections were right.

name: bnxt_ptp_enable
prose: ptp_clock_info enable callback (bnxt_ptp.c:476-533); ptp_info is the member of a valid bnxt_ptp_cfg, rq is the request and 'on' enables (non-zero) or disables (0). For PTP_CLK_REQ_EXTTS and PTP_CLK_REQ_PEROUT it looks the pin up with ptp_find_pin and returns -EOPNOTSUPP if TSIO_PIN_VALID rejects it. For EXTTS with on set it calls bnxt_ptp_cfg_pin(PPS_IN) and returns its error if non-zero, then bnxt_ptp_cfg_event(EXTERNAL) and, only if that succeeds, caches the event in ptp->pps_info.pins[pin_id].event; it returns that rc. For PEROUT with on set it calls bnxt_ptp_cfg_pin(PPS_OUT) and, only if that succeeded, bnxt_ptp_perout_cfg(ptp, rq) and returns the resulting rc (no event is cached for PEROUT). For PTP_CLK_REQ_PPS (pin_id 0, no pin lookup) with on set it does the same as EXTTS but with BNXT_PPS_PIN_PPS_IN and BNXT_PPS_EVENT_INTERNAL. When on is 0 these three cases do not return directly but break out and reach the final statement, which returns bnxt_ptp_cfg_pin(bp, pin_id, BNXT_PPS_PIN_NONE) (line 532), i.e. the pin is reset to NONE and that call's result is returned. Any other rq->type logs 'Unrecognized PIN function' and returns -EOPNOTSUPP.
note: Reviewers: original and round-15 ('on=0 returns 0 without configuring' / 'on=0 break and return 0') are WRONG: after break the function returns bnxt_ptp_cfg_pin(...PIN_NONE) at 532. Round-15 'default does not log' is WRONG (528 logs). Round-2 'omits cfg_pin failure return' is right for the old prose (494-496, 510-514); its 'event caching for PEROUT' is wrong (PEROUT caches nothing). Slice cut the head; real function 476-533. Tally: 1 right (partly), 3 wrong.

name: bnxt_ulp_stop
prose: Marks every registered auxiliary-device slot as stopped and suspends its bound driver (bnxt_ulp.c:268-304). It holds bp->auxdev_lock for the whole loop and, for each slot i below __BNXT_AUXDEV_MAX, skips slots that bnxt_auxdev_is_active reports inactive. For an active slot it takes edev->en_dev_lock and, if the edev is not registered (bnxt_ulp_registered false) or BNXT_EN_FLAG_ULP_STOPPED is already set, it releases en_dev_lock and moves on, changing nothing. Otherwise it sets BNXT_EN_FLAG_ULP_STOPPED in edev->flags (this happens whether or not a driver is bound); then, only if adev->dev.driver is non-NULL, it sets edev->en_state = bp->state and calls that auxiliary driver's suspend(adev, pm) callback with an empty pm_message, all while holding en_dev_lock; it then releases en_dev_lock. It has no return value and does not check that the driver has a suspend callback.
note: Reviewers: original and round-2 (suspend and en_state only when a driver is bound) right: 293-299; round-15 (registered slots without a driver still get the STOPPED flag) right: 290 is before the driver test. 3/3 right.

name: bcmgenet_wol_power_up_cfg
prose: Undoes the Wake-on-LAN power-down configuration of a GENET MAC (bcmgenet_wol.c, function starting 'int bcmgenet_wol_power_up_cfg', about line 218-278; the slice shows only the tail). If mode is not GENET_POWER_WOL_MAGIC it logs and returns -EINVAL without touching hardware. Otherwise it disables and unprepares priv->clk_wol, clears priv->crc_fwd_en, masks the wake-event interrupt (and unmasks the MDIO event if the chip has an MDIO interrupt). If wolopts contains WAKE_MAGIC or WAKE_MAGICSECURE it reads UMAC_MPD_CTRL and returns -EPERM (the rest skipped, but the clock, crc_fwd_en and interrupt-mask changes above already done) when MPD_EN is not set, else clears MPD_EN and MPD_PW_EN. It then reads HFB_CTRL and returns -EPERM when RBUF_ACPI_EN is not set, else clears it. Under reg_lock (spin_lock_bh) it clears CMD_CRC_FWD in UMAC_CMD, re-reads UMAC_CMD and, if CMD_RX_EN is set and CMD_TX_EN is not, sets CMD_SW_RESET; it unlocks reg_lock, then under the PHY mutex sets phydev->state to PHY_RUNNING if phydev->link is set, otherwise PHY_NOLINK, and returns 0.
note: Slice has no head but the function exists; fixed under real name per rule 6 (read 218-278 of bcmgenet_wol.c). Old 'dropped' prose said 'returns 0' only; the -EINVAL/-EPERM paths were missing.

name: tg3_test_dma
prose: Chooses the TG3PCI_DMA_RW_CTRL value and, on 5700/5701 chips only, runs a DMA write/read-back test (tg3.c:17364-17536; slice cut the head). It first allocates a coherent TEST_BUFFER_SIZE buffer; if that fails it returns -ENOMEM through out_nofree, without calling dma_free_coherent. Otherwise it computes tp->dma_rwctrl (command bits, tg3_calc_dma_bndry, and chip- and bus-mode-specific watermark bits). For 57765_PLUS chips it jumps to out immediately, after setting tp->dma_rwctrl in memory but without writing TG3PCI_DMA_RW_CTRL. For all other chips it writes TG3PCI_DMA_RW_CTRL (17452); if the chip is not 5700 or 5701 it then goes to out and returns 0. On 5700/5701 it clears the write boundary bits, then loops: fill the buffer with a counting pattern, DMA it to the chip and back with tg3_do_test_dma (write or read failure logs and breaks with that error), compare; on the first mismatch it sets the write boundary to 16 bytes, rewrites the register and retries, but if the boundary is already 16 it logs 'Buffer corrupted on read back!' and goes to out with ret = -ENODEV. When the pattern verifies, ret = 0; if the boundary was never reduced, it sets the boundary to 16 when a chipset listed in tg3_dma_wait_state_chipsets is present, otherwise restores the saved value, and rewrites the register. At out (reached on every path except the allocation failure) it frees the buffer and returns ret, which is 0, -ENODEV, or the error from tg3_do_test_dma.
note: Reviewer (57765_PLUS path skips programming TG3PCI_DMA_RW_CTRL, allocation-failure path skips dma_free_coherent) is right: 17382-17383 and 17372-17375. Note a read/write failure break skips the final boundary/chipset block and still frees. Slice cut the head.

name: tg3_setup_copper_phy
prose: Brings up the copper PHY link and programs the MAC to match (tg3.c:4763-5114; the packet name tg3_setup_copper_link does not exist and the slice cut the head). force_reset forces a PHY reset. It clears MAC status, turns off MI auto-poll if on, writes the PWRCTL aux-control shadow register, and resets the PHY when force_reset is set or when a 5703/5704/5705 with tp->link_up reads BMSR link-down. For a BCM5401 PHY with no link it runs tg3_init_5401phy_dsp and returns that error if non-zero; on a B0 revision with 1000 Mb/s active speed and still no link it also does tg3_phy_reset then tg3_init_5401phy_dsp and returns an error from either. These are the only error returns: every other path ends with 'return 0' (about line 5112), so it returns an error code only from those 5401 DSP/reset paths. It then clears pending PHY interrupts, sets the interrupt mask, applies 5700/5701 LED setup, and polls BMSR (up to 100 times), reads the aux status (up to 2000 times) and BMCR (up to 200 times). It decides current_link_up from the autonegotiation configuration (EEE/advert checks, may call tg3_setup_eee and tg3_phy_reset if EEE config is not OK and link flap avoidance skipped the reset) or from the forced speed/duplex, records MDIX state and calls tg3_setup_flow_control for a full-duplex link. If no link (or the PHY is low power) it calls tg3_phy_copper_begin, forces the link up for ROBOSWITCH, and sets link up again if BMSR shows link or MAC_MODE_PORT_INT_LPBACK is set. It then rewrites tp->mac_mode (port mode MII/GMII, half duplex bit, 5700 link polarity), sets RGMII LED control if RGMII mode, applies BCM5411/5700-Altima and 5700 1000 Mb/s PCI-X workarounds, writes MAC_MODE and MAC_EVENT (0 when USE_LINKCHG_REG is set, otherwise MAC_EVENT_LNKSTATE_CHANGED), sets or clears CLKREQ_EN in the PCIe link control when the CLKREQ_BUG flag is set, calls tg3_phy_eee_adjust and tg3_test_and_report_link_chg, and returns 0.
note: Slice cut the head (real function tg3_setup_copper_phy 4763-5114; packet name wrong). Old prose 'returns 0' lacked the err returns at 4812 and 4829 region. Old reviewers only mechanical ('name not in slice'), right.

name: BFA_SM_TABLE(n, s, e, t)
prose: Macro that, for each instantiation, defines a state-machine function-pointer typedef t, a table-entry struct n_sm_table_s and the generated function 'static inline int n_sm_to_state(struct n_sm_table_s *smt, t sm)' (bfa_cs.h:22-41; instantiated ten times at lines 43-53, e.g. ioc_sm_to_state). The generated function walks smt from index 0 while smt[i].sm is non-NULL and differs from sm, then returns smt[i].state of the entry where it stopped. If sm is found it returns the state encoding of the first matching entry; if it is not found it returns the state field of the terminating entry (the one whose sm is NULL), whatever value that holds. smt must therefore be an array terminated by an entry with sm == NULL; without such a terminator the loop reads past the array. It has no side effects.
note: Macro-generated function: name given as the macro definition head, prose names the generated function (rule 5). Old prose (unreviewed) did not say what is returned when sm is absent.

name: bfa_mfg_adapter_prop_init_gpio
prose: Statement macro (do { } while (0)) in bfa_defs_mfg_comm.h:73-104 that derives the adapter property word and card type from a GPIO value. It evaluates its arguments several times, so gpio, card_type and prop must be modifiable side-effect-free lvalues. If gpio has the CB_GPIO_PROTO bit set it ORs BFI_ADAPTER_PROTO into prop and clears CB_GPIO_PROTO in gpio (modifying the caller's gpio variable). It then switches on gpio: CB_GPIO_TTV ORs BFI_ADAPTER_TTV into prop and falls through to the CB_GPIO_DFLY / CB_GPIO_FC8P2 case; DFLY, FC8P2 and TTV all OR in 2 ports and speed 8 (BFI_ADAPTER_SETP) and set card_type = BFA_MFG_TYPE_FC8P2; CB_GPIO_FC8P1 ORs in 1 port, speed 8, card_type FC8P1; CB_GPIO_FC4P2 ORs 2 ports, speed 4, card_type FC4P2; CB_GPIO_FC4P1 ORs 1 port, speed 4, card_type FC4P1; any other value ORs BFI_ADAPTER_UNSUPP into prop and sets card_type = BFA_MFG_TYPE_INVALID. prop is only OR-ed into, never cleared, so bits already present in it remain. The previous Frama-C-style contract was unsound for that reason and is removed.
note: Item is a function-like statement macro, not a function; kept as a fix because it carries real logic. Contract left empty (the old one fails when prop already has the UNSUPP bit).

name: bna_tx_sm_stopped
prose: State handler for the TX object in the stopped state (bna_tx_rx.c:2806-2827; slice cut the head; the packet name bfa_fsm_tx_sm_stop does not exist). tx is the TX object and event a bna_tx_event. TX_E_START changes the state with bfa_fsm_set_state(tx, bna_tx_sm_start_wait) (which runs that state's entry function); TX_E_STOP calls call_tx_stop_cbfn(tx) and stays in this state; TX_E_FAIL and TX_E_BW_UPDATE are ignored; any other event calls bfa_sm_fault, which only logs 'SM Assertion failure' with pr_err and does not stop execution. Returns nothing.
note: Slice began mid-function (head and TX_E_START case at 2806-2812 not shown); fixed under the real name per rule 6. Old prose omitted TX_E_START.

name: macb_probe
prose: Platform-driver probe for a Cadence MACB/GEM Ethernet controller (macb_main.c:5556-5777; the slice cut the head). It returns the error from devm_platform_get_and_ioremap_resource (5578) or from the config's clk_init callback (5593) before any runtime-PM setup. After that it enables runtime PM (autosuspend delay set, pm_runtime_get_noresume, set_active, enable), probes the queue count, allocates the net_device (-ENOMEM on failure, jumping to err_disable_clocks), fills struct macb from the device-tree match data (default_gem_config otherwise) and from DCFG registers, sets the 44-bit DMA mask when the hardware reports 64-bit addressing, gets the IRQ, sets the MAC address (a deferred-probe error from of_get_ethdev_address goes to cleanup; any other error falls back to macb_get_hwaddr) and the PHY interface mode (MII when not in the device tree), then calls the config's init callback and macb_mii_init and register_netdev. Error labels in order: err_out_unregister_mdio (unregister/free the MDIO bus if present and phylink_destroy), err_out_phy_exit (phy_exit), err_out_free_netdev (free_netdev), err_disable_clocks (macb_clks_disable, pm_runtime_disable, pm_runtime_set_suspended, pm_runtime_dont_use_autosuspend), then it returns the saved error. The failure path never calls pm_runtime_put_noidle for the earlier pm_runtime_get_noresume reference; it only disables runtime PM and marks the device suspended. On success it logs the device info, calls pm_runtime_mark_last_busy and pm_runtime_put_autosuspend and returns 0.
note: Reviewer (failure path never calls pm_runtime_put_noidle) is right: 5770-5776 only disable/set_suspended/dont_use_autosuspend. Slice cut the head; real function 5556-5777.

name: lio_ethtool_set_ringparam
prose: ethtool set-ring-parameters handler for LiquidIO (lio_ethtool.c, function head 'lio_ethtool_set_ringparam' at about line 1258; the packet name lio_set_ringparam is not the real name). Returns -EINVAL if the device is neither a CN23XX PF nor a CN23XX VF, or if rx_mini_pending or rx_jumbo_pending is non-zero. Otherwise it clamps ering->rx_pending and tx_pending to the CN23XX min/max descriptor counts and compares them with oct->droq[0]->max_count and oct->instr_queue[0]->max_count; if both are unchanged it returns 0 without doing anything. Otherwise it sets LIO_IFSTATE_RESETTING, calls ndo_stop if the netdev is running (remembering that), stores the new TX and RX descriptor counts in the NIC interface config for whichever changed, and calls lio_reset_queues(netdev, oct->num_iqs). If that returns non-zero it goes to err_lio_reset_queues, which restores the old counts in the config and returns -EINVAL; in that failure case LIO_IFSTATE_RESETTING is not cleared and ndo_open is not called again, so a device that was stopped stays stopped. On success it calls ndo_open if it had stopped the device (the return value of ndo_open is not checked), clears LIO_IFSTATE_RESETTING and returns 0.
note: Slice began inside the function and the packet name is wrong; real function lio_ethtool_set_ringparam. Old prose not checked against the failure path (RESETTING not cleared, no reopen).

name: octeon_device_init
prose: Brings up one LiquidIO (OCTEON) device on the PF side (lio_main.c:4019-4292; slice cut the head, the packet's unnamed item is this function). It returns 1 for most failures and returns the callee's own non-zero value for failures of setup_device_regs (both the PF and non-PF branch) and enable_io_queues. In order: set status to OCT_DEV_BEGIN_STATE; octeon_pci_os_setup (return 1 on failure); chip-specific setup (return 1); registers the device and, for a CN23XX PF with firmware already loaded and fw_type auto, marks the adapter firmware state as preloaded via a compare-and-swap; takes FW_NEEDS_TO_BE_LOADED to FW_IS_BEING_LOADED with another cmpxchg and keeps the previous state in fw_state; if this instance must load firmware it soft-resets the device (return 1 on failure); initialises the dispatch list (return 1 on failure, before the delayed work is scheduled), registers two dispatch functions, schedules the nic_starter delayed work and sets OCT_DEV_DISPATCH_INIT_DONE; then sets IO queues off, sets up device registers (PF), the soft-command buffer pool, instruction queues, response list, output queues, and (PF) mailbox and ioq vectors, sets up the droq tasklet and interrupts, enables interrupts, credits the output queues and enables the IO queues, advancing the status value after each stage. If fw_state was FW_NEEDS_TO_BE_LOADED it also waits for DDR init (returning 1 if a signal interrupts the wait while ddr_timeout is zero, or if DDR init/bootloader/console setup fails), then loads firmware and marks the adapter state FW_HAS_BEEN_LOADED; load failure returns 1. On success it sets handshake[octeon_id].init_ok = 1, completes handshake init, sets status OCT_DEV_HOST_OK, stores the device in oct_priv->dev and returns 0. It does no cleanup of its own on error: resources created so far are left for the caller's destroy path, which relies on the status value, and the delayed work stays scheduled once past line 4105.
note: Reviewer (init_dispatch_list failure occurs before the delayed work is scheduled) is right: 4092-4093 vs 4103-4106. Slice cut the head; real function octeon_device_init 4019-4292.

name: liquidio_xmit
prose: ndo_start_xmit for the LiquidIO VF (lio_vf_main.c:1407-1629; the packet item 'lio_xmit_fragment_loop' is only the scatter-gather loop inside this function). Returns NETDEV_TX_BUSY in these cases: the instruction queue is full (counts tx_iq_busy), or a DMA mapping fails (head of a linear skb, the linear part of a gather skb, or a page fragment). In those mapping-failure returns it does not free the skb; for a fragment mapping error it first unmaps the linear part and the fragments already mapped, but the gather-list entry taken from lio->glist has not been put back on that list. It returns NETDEV_TX_OK when the packet is queued, and also after the lio_xmit_failed path, which drops the packet. lio_xmit_failed is taken when the interface is not running, the link is down, skb->len <= 0, no gather entry is available (glist empty), or the send (octnet_send_nic_data_pkt or send_nic_timestamp_pkt) returns IQ_SEND_FAILED; it increments stats->tx_dropped, unmaps dptr with dma_unmap_single if dptr is non-zero, rings the doorbell, frees the skb with tx_buffer_free and returns NETDEV_TX_OK. For a non-linear skb the loop maps each fragment into g->sg and, on a mapping failure, unmaps earlier mappings before returning NETDEV_TX_BUSY. On success it also sets GSO size/segments and VLAN priority/id in the command, stops the subqueue when the send returns IQ_SEND_STOP, updates the tx_done (by gso_segs when non-zero) and tx_tot_bytes counters, and returns NETDEV_TX_OK.
note: Item named lio_xmit_fragment_loop is a fragment of liquidio_xmit; fixed under the real name per rule 6 (read 1407-1629 in full). Old prose said the failure case returns NETDEV_TX_BUSY with earlier mappings unwound, which only covers the fragment-mapping branch; other paths differ.

name: octeon_device_init
prose: Initialises a LiquidIO CN23XX virtual function (lio_vf_main.c:2281-2371; the packet's unnamed item is this function). It sets the status to OCT_DEV_BEGIN_STATE, runs octeon_pci_os_setup, records chip id CN23XX_VF and the revision byte, and calls cn23xx_setup_octeon_vf_device, which is what fills in oct->fn_list and sriov_info (they are not set by the caller). It then advances oct->status through the stages as each succeeds: dispatch list, IO queues off, setup_device_regs, soft-command buffer pool, instruction queues, response list, output queues, mailbox, ioq vector allocation (rings_per_vf), interrupt setup, enable interrupts, PF-VF handshake (cn23xx_octeon_pfvf_handshake), interrupts re-enabled, enable_io_queues, then status OCT_DEV_HOST_OK, output-queue credits written to each droq's pkts_credit_reg, OCT_DEV_CORE_OK, OCT_DEV_RUNNING, and finally liquidio_init_nic_module. Every failing step returns 1 immediately, with no cleanup in this function (the caller's teardown uses oct->status); the final return value is 0 only when liquidio_init_nic_module returns 0, and 1 otherwise.
note: Reviewer (precondition wrongly says fn_list and rings_per_vf are caller-set; cn23xx_setup_octeon_vf_device sets them) is right: 2295-2297 then use of fn_list at 2316. Slice cut the head; real function starts 2281.

name: get_sset_count
prose: ethtool get_sset_count callback of the cxgb driver (cxgb2.c:437-445). dev is unused. If sset is ETH_SS_STATS it returns ARRAY_SIZE(stats_strings), which is 58 entries in the table at cxgb2.c:354-419; for any other sset it returns -EOPNOTSUPP (-95). It reads no mutable state and takes no locks.

name: cxgb_ioctl
prose: ndo_eth_ioctl handler of the cxgb3 driver (cxgb3_main.c:2530-2552; the slice cut the head). It switches on cmd. For SIOCGMIIREG and SIOCSMIIREG, if the adapter is 10G (is_10G) and data->phy_id is not already a clause-45 id, has bits in 0x1f00 and none in 0xe0e0, it rewrites data->phy_id into clause-45 form from the old PRTAD/DEVAD layout (mdio_phy_id_c45(phy_id >> 8, phy_id & 0x1f)); it then falls through. For those two and for SIOCGMIIPHY it returns mdio_mii_ioctl(&pi->phy.mdio, data, cmd), i.e. the result of the generic MDIO helper. Any other cmd returns -EOPNOTSUPP. The CHELSIO_* private commands are not handled here; they are handled by the separate ndo_siocdevprivate function cxgb_siocdevprivate (line 2133).
note: Reviewer (omits CHELSIO_* commands; other cmd not always -EOPNOTSUPP) is WRONG for this function: the switch at 2536-2551 has only the MII cases and default -EOPNOTSUPP; CHELSIO_* are in cxgb_siocdevprivate at 2133. Slice cut the head; real function 2530-2552.

name: adap_init0
prose: Connects the cxgb4 driver to the adapter firmware, initialises the adapter if needed and reads the firmware-provisioned resources into struct adapter (cxgb4_main.c:4752-5414; slice cut the head). vpd_skip non-zero skips reading VPD parameters. Early returns before any allocation: the negative error from t4_init_devlog_params (4766), from t4_fw_hello (4774, logged 'could not connect to FW'), and -EINVAL when no firmware info exists for the chip while acting as master PF with the device not initialised (4807). Every later failure sets ret and goes to bye: -ENOMEM when kvzalloc of the card firmware header fails; t4_prep_fw returning < 0 (the firmware image is released first; a failing request_firmware is only logged and then t4_prep_fw runs with no image); the configuration-file query failing (no firmware config-file support), adap_init0_config returning -ENOENT or < 0 (only when the device was not already initialised); t4_get_pfres, t4_get_vpd_params (unless vpd_skip), the port-vector query, t4_sge_init, the basic PF/VF parameter queries (EQ/L2T/filter/IQFLINT start/end, EQ_END/IQFLINT_END), -ENOMEM from allocating egr_map, ingr_map and the starving_fl, txq_maperr (and blocked_fl with CONFIG_DEBUG_FS) bitmaps, the CLIP range query, the FW_CAPS_CONFIG_CMD mailbox read, and, depending on the capabilities the firmware reports, the offload (NTID, server, TDDP, flow control), RDMA, iSCSI and crypto/TLS parameter queries (a crypto-lookaside query failing with -EINVAL is tolerated). Several queries are not fatal: if the number-of-traffic-classes query fails nsched_cls is hard-coded to 15 (T4) or 16; the active-filter range, ULPTX memwrite DSGL, FW_RI_FR_NSMR_TPTE_WR, FILTER2, OPAQUE_VIID_SMT_EXTN, RDMA write-with-immediate / write-completion queries only set flags when they succeed with a non-zero value; the T6 raw-filter, ETHOFLD, SRQ and PPOD EDRAM queries are used only if they succeed; the MAXORDIRD/MAXIRD query falls back to 8 and 32*ntids; and the CPLFW4MSG_ENCAP set-params result is ignored. When the device was not already initialised it also edits the MTU table (changing an MTU of 1492 to 1488) and loads it. At bye it frees the HMA memory, egr_map, ingr_map, the bitmaps, and calls t4_fw_bye unless ret is -ETIMEDOUT or -EIO, then returns ret. The success path calls t4_init_sge_params, sets CXGB4_FW_OK in adap->flags, calls t4_init_tp_params and returns 0 (5395). In the already-initialised state (DEV_STATE_INIT) it only calls adap_config_hma, logging but ignoring its failure.
note: Reviewer (postcondition claims traffic-class/offload params retrieved but code hardcodes or ignores failed queries and can return 0) is right: 5069-5079 hardcodes nsched_cls, 5084-5092, 5101, 5112-5141 ignore failures. Read the whole 663-line function (4752-5414). Slice cut the head.

name: init_one
prose: PCI probe for a Chelsio T4/T5/T6 adapter (cxgb4_main.c:6571-7070; the packet name cxgb4_init_one is not the real name and the slice cut the head). It first claims the PCI regions (error returned directly), enables the device, maps BAR0 and allocates the adapter, mailbox log and, if needed, the workqueue; it waits for the device, identifies the chip and the PF number and stores them. If the PF number (func) differs from ent->driver_data it disables the PCI device, saves PCI state and returns 0 at once (6653), leaving the adapter allocated as drvdata without registering anything. Otherwise it sets the 64-bit DMA mask, bus mastering, creates the workqueue, prepares the adapter (t4_prep_adapter), on non-T4 chips validates the egress-queues-per-page value (-EINVAL if it exceeds the segments per page) and maps BAR2 write-combining (-ENOMEM on failure), sets up memory windows and calls adap_init0; a failure there goes to out_unmap_bar. It then allocates one net_device per port (-ENOMEM goes to out_free_dev), sets features and ops, and, if the firmware connection is up, calls t4_port_init (failure goes to out_free_dev) and configures queues (cfg_queues), SMT, L2T, CLIP, scheduling and TID tables, TC offloads, interrupts, RSS, non-data interrupts and firmware SGE queues; failures of cfg_queues, init_rss, setup_non_data_intr and setup_fw_sge_queues go to out_free_dev, while failures to allocate SMT, L2T, CLIP, the TID table or TC offloads are only warned about (clearing params.offload for the L2T/CLIP/TID cases). If the firmware is not OK it skips all that (label fw_attach_fail) and, with one port, tries to read the MAC address from raw VPD. It then registers each port's net_device; if none registers it goes to out_free_dev, and if only some do it warns and continues with err = 0. On success it creates debugfs entries when cxgb4_debugfs_root is set, enables ULDs and PTP/thermal where applicable, prints adapter info and returns 0. The error labels unwind in this order: out_free_dev (free SGE resources and other resources, MSI-X info, ULD memory), out_unmap_bar (iounmap BAR2 on non-T4), out_free_adapter (destroy workqueue, free mbox_log and adapter), out_unmap_bar0, out_disable_device, out_release_regions; the function returns err after the matching tail.
note: Packet name wrong and slice cut the head; real init_one 6571-7070, read in full. Previous mechanical rejections ('name not in slice') were right. Note the 'func != driver_data' early return of 0 with allocated adapter (6650-6654).

name: cxgb4_setup_tc_mqprio
prose: Applies a TC mqprio offload request to a cxgb4 port (cxgb4_tc_mqprio.c:573-626; the slice shows more than this function). It first calls cxgb4_mqprio_validate(dev, mqprio) and returns its non-zero result immediately, before taking any lock. Otherwise it takes adap->tc_mqprio->mqprio_mutex, and if the netdev is running stops all TX queues, turns the carrier off and remembers to bring it back. It then calls cxgb4_mqprio_disable_offload(dev) unconditionally. If mqprio->qopt.num_tc is 0 it goes to out with ret still 0, so a successful 'clear' request leaves no mqprio offload configured. Otherwise it calls cxgb4_mqprio_alloc_tc; if that fails it goes to out with its error without calling cxgb4_mqprio_free_tc in this function. Then it calls cxgb4_mqprio_enable_offload; if that fails it calls cxgb4_mqprio_free_tc and goes to out. At out it restarts the TX queues and turns the carrier back on if it had stopped them (also on the failure paths), unlocks the mutex and returns ret, which is 0 on success or the error of the failed step. The mutex is released on every path that acquired it; only the validation-failure return happens before the lock.
note: Reviewers: original (num_tc=0 success leaves no config active) right; round-2 (validate failure returns before mutex_lock) right as a fact (580-582), prose now states it; round-15 (alloc_tc failure does not free classes here, only enable_offload failure does) right for this function (608-616). 3/3 right.

name: t4_load_boot
prose: Writes (or erases) the expansion-ROM boot image in adapter flash (t4_hw.c:10569-10675; slice cut the head). boot_data holds the image, boot_addr is the flash offset in KiB (boot_sector = boot_addr * 1024) and size the image length in bytes. Returns -EFBIG if (boot_sector + size) >> 16 is above FLASH_FW_START_SEC, i.e. the image would run into the firmware region (10584-10587), and also -EFBIG if size is below BOOT_MIN_SIZE or above BOOT_MAX_SIZE (BOOT_MIN_SIZE is the size of the ROM header, so size 0 is rejected here as well; the later 'size == 0' erase-only test is therefore not reachable with size 0). Returns -EINVAL when the ROM header signature, the PCIR signature, or the PCIR vendor id (must be PCI_VENDOR_ID_CHELSIO) do not match. These checks read the header and PCIR structure from boot_data using the offset stored in the image (pcir_offset), which is not bounds-checked against size. It then erases the flash sectors that cover the image with t4_flash_erase_sectors; if the erase fails it goes to out. Otherwise it reads the adapter's PCI device id (masking with 0xf0ff) and, if the image's PCIR device id differs, rewrites it in the image buffer with modify_device_id (so boot_data is modified). It writes the image page by page (SF_PAGE_SIZE bytes) starting from the second page via t4_write_flash, stopping at the first error, and writes the first page (the BIOS header) last; the loop assumes size is a multiple of SF_PAGE_SIZE and nothing checks that. At out it logs 'boot image load failed' if ret is non-zero and returns ret (the error from the erase or flash write, or 0).
note: Reviewer (no FLASH_FW_START check; only size range returns -EFBIG) is WRONG: 10584-10587 return -EFBIG when the image encroaches on the firmware region, in addition to the size check at 10600. Slice cut the head; real function 10569-10675. BOOT_MIN_SIZE = sizeof(rom header) at cxgb4.h:200.

name: t4vf_handle_get_port_info
prose: Processes a firmware Port Information reply for a VF port and updates the port's link state (t4vf_hw.c:1913-2057; slice cut the head). pi and cmd must be valid, pi->adapter valid. It decodes the action from cmd->action_to_len16. For FW_PORT_ACTION_GET_PORT_INFO it extracts link status, link-down reason, port type, module type and the 16-bit capabilities (converted to 32-bit) and builds the link attributes from the status bits; for FW_PORT_ACTION_GET_PORT_INFO32 it takes the same values from the 32-bit message. Any other action logs 'Bad Command/Action' with dev_err and returns without changing anything; so an unrecognised action is tolerated, not a precondition violation. It then computes the FEC, advertised and negotiated pause and speed. If the module type differs from pi->mod_type it sets lc->auto_fec, pi->port_type and pi->mod_type and calls t4vf_os_portmod_changed. Next, only if link_ok, speed, fc, advertised_fc or fec differ from what is stored in pi->link_cfg, it: records lc->link_down_rc and logs a rate-limited warning only when the link has just gone down (!link_ok && lc->link_ok); stores link_ok, speed, advertised_fc, fc, fec, pcaps, lpacaps and acaps (masked with ADVERT_MASK); sets lc->autoneg to AUTONEG_DISABLE if the port is not capable of autonegotiation, to AUTONEG_ENABLE if the advertised capabilities include it, and otherwise to AUTONEG_DISABLE after clearing lc->acaps and setting lc->speed_caps from the advertised speed; and finally calls t4vf_os_link_changed. When nothing in that list changed, none of those link_config fields are modified (but lc->auto_fec, pi->port_type and pi->mod_type may still have been updated by the module-type branch). It returns nothing.
note: Reviewers: original (unknown action is logged and ignored, not a precondition) right: 1978-1982; round-2 (link_down_rc/speed_caps only conditionally updated; omits auto_fec) right: 2019-2025, 2050-2051, 1997; round-15 (auto_fec set when mod_type differs even if link values unchanged) right: 1989-1997. 3/3 right.

name: chtls_sendmsg
prose: sendmsg handler for a Chelsio inline-TLS/TOE socket (chtls_io.c:1010-1240; slice cut the head). The caller must not hold the socket lock: the function takes lock_sock(sk) at entry and releases it at the done label, so every return goes through release_sock. It waits for the connection if the socket is not ESTABLISHED/CLOSE_WAIT (error from sk_stream_wait_connect goes to out_err) and goes to out_err with -EPIPE if sk_err is set or SEND_SHUTDOWN is on. In the loop it appends data to the tail skb of csk->txq or allocates a new skb (get_tx_skb, or get_record_skb for TLS), copies data into the skb tailroom, or into page fragments (coalescing, new pages of order cdev->send_page_order falling back to a single page), or splices pages when MSG_SPLICE_PAGES is set; for TLS records it takes a record size, may parse control messages (chtls_proccess_cmsg, error to out_err) and limits each copy to csk->tlshws.txleft. It waits for memory or send-buffer space with csk_wait_memory (error to do_error). Exit paths: when all data is copied (size == 0) it goes to out, clears CSK_TX_MORE_DATA, calls chtls_tcp_push if anything was copied, and returns the number of bytes copied. do_fault (copy error) frees an empty tail skb and falls into do_error: if some data was already copied it goes to out and returns copied (after chtls_tcp_push), without calling sk_stream_error; with nothing copied it falls to out_err, which clears CSK_TX_MORE_DATA for an inline connection and returns sk_stream_error(sk, flags, err). out_err is also reached directly (connect wait, shutdown/sk_err, cmsg failure); in those cases the return value is sk_stream_error's result even if bytes were copied earlier (possible for a cmsg failure on a later TLS record). The function updates tp->write_seq, sk_wmem_queued, TCP_PAGE/TCP_OFF and the TLS tx-left counters as it goes.
note: Reviewer (sk_stream_error not called when copied > 0; code returns copied after chtls_tcp_push) is right for the do_error path (1232-1234, 1219-1225). Not mentioned by reviewer: out_err reached directly with copied > 0 overrides the return value (1235-1238). Slice cut the head; real function 1010-1240.

name: sundance_probe1
prose: PCI probe for a Sundance/D-Link fast-ethernet chip (sundance.c:492-705; the packet name sundance_probe is not the real name and the slice cut the head). pci_enable_device failure returns -EIO and alloc_etherdev failure returns -ENOMEM, before anything else is set up. After that every failure returns -ENODEV through the unwind chain err_out_unregister (unregister_netdev), err_out_unmap_rx (free the RX descriptor ring), err_out_unmap_tx (free the TX ring), err_out_cleardev (pci_iounmap), err_out_res (pci_release_regions), err_out_netdev (free_netdev); each failing step enters the chain at the label that frees exactly the resources acquired so far: pci_request_regions failing (err_out_netdev), pci_iomap failing (err_out_res), TX ring dma_alloc_coherent failing (err_out_cleardev), RX ring allocation failing (err_out_unmap_tx), register_netdev failing (err_out_unmap_rx), and no MII transceiver found (err_out_unregister). It reads the MAC address from the EEPROM, sets up the net_device, registers it, scans MII PHY addresses (skipping address 0 first unless the device id is 0x0200), parses the media override module parameters, resets and restarts the PHY (300 ms delay), optionally forces speed/duplex, resets the chip and returns 0 after incrementing card_idx. The error chain never calls pci_disable_device for the device enabled at the start, and pci_set_drvdata(pdev, dev) is done before register_netdev, so on later failures the PCI drvdata still points at the net_device that is then freed.
note: Reviewer (failure paths leave drvdata pointing at freed dev, and do not free both rings) is mixed: drvdata dangling is right (576 set, never cleared at 690-704); 'do not free both rings' is wrong, each label frees the rings allocated so far and err_out_unmap_rx frees RX then TX. I also found pci_disable_device is never called on failure. Slice cut the head; real function 492-705.

name: enetc_setup_tc_cbs
prose: Configures (or disables) credit-based shaping for one traffic class of an ENETC port (enetc_qos.c:234-348; slice cut the head). type_data is a struct tc_cbs_qopt_offload; the class is cbs->queue, and only the two numerically highest classes (netdev_get_num_tc - 1 and - 2) are supported, otherwise it returns -EOPNOTSUPP. Disable request (cbs->enable == 0): if tc is the top class and the next class is still enabled (enetc_get_cbs_enable reads the hardware) it logs and returns -EINVAL; otherwise it writes 0 to ENETC_PTCCBSR1 and ENETC_PTCCBSR0 for tc and returns 0. Enable request: it returns -EOPNOTSUPP unless idleslope - sendslope equals port rate (priv->speed) * 1000, idleslope >= 0 and sendslope <= 0. It computes bw = idleslope / (speed * 10); for the second class it first reads the hardware and returns -EINVAL if the top class is not enabled, then adds the top class's configured bandwidth (read from hardware); it returns -EINVAL if the total bandwidth including this class is 100 or more. It then computes the maximum interference size (frame size for the top class; for the second class from the top class's max-SDU register and bandwidth), derives the hiCredit values, writes ENETC_PTCCBSR1 (hiCredit) and ENETC_PTCCBSR0 (bw | ENETC_CBSE) and returns 0. The -EINVAL paths (and the bandwidth check) do read hardware registers first via enetc_get_cbs_enable/enetc_get_cbs_bw and the MSDU register, but no register is written on any of them; hardware writes happen only on the two successful paths above.
note: Reviewer (-EINVAL paths read CBS enable/bandwidth registers first, so they do touch hardware) is right about reads: 261, 286, 292; but no writes occur before those returns. Prose now says reads happen and writes do not. Slice cut the head; real function 234-348.

name: fec_probe
prose: Platform-driver probe for a Freescale/NXP FEC Ethernet controller (fec_main.c:4391-4671; the packet name fec_drv_probe is not the real name and the slice shows only the tail). It returns -ENOMEM if alloc_etherdev_mqs fails (before anything else); every later failure sets ret and jumps to a cleanup label, and the function ends with free_netdev(ndev) and returns ret. Steps and their failure labels: ioremap of the registers (failed_ioremap), fec_enet_ipc_handle_init (failed_ipc_init), fec_enet_init_stop_mode (failed_stop_mode), registering a fixed-link PHY (failed_phy), parsing RGMII delays (failed_rgmii_delay), getting the ipg, ahb, enet_out and enet_clk_ref clocks (failed_clk; the 2x_txclk and ptp clocks are optional, a missing ptp clock disables extended buffer descriptors), fec_enet_clk_enable (failed_clk), enabling the ipg and ahb clocks (failed_clk_ipg, failed_clk_ahb), enabling the optional PHY regulator (failed_regulator; -EPROBE_DEFER is propagated, other lookup errors mean no regulator), then runtime PM is enabled, fec_reset_phy (failed_reset), fec_enet_init (failed_init), requesting each interrupt line (failed_irq), fec_enet_mii_init (failed_mii_init) and register_netdev (failed_register). The labels unwind in order: fec_enet_mii_remove, fec_enet_deinit, fec_ptp_stop (if extended descriptors), pm_runtime_put_noidle and pm_runtime_disable, regulator disable, ahb and ipg clock disable, fec_enet_clk_enable(false), deregistering a fixed-link PHY and of_node_put(phy_node), decrementing dev_id, then free_netdev. Before register_netdev it turns the clocks off again (fec_enet_clk_enable(ndev, false)) and selects the sleep pinctrl state, so a successful probe leaves the clocks gated until the interface is opened; it sets the carrier off and max_mtu. On success it initialises wakeup from the 'fsl,magic-packet' flag, sets up the timeout work, releases the runtime-PM reference with pm_runtime_put_autosuspend and returns 0 (4637).
note: Packet name wrong and slice cut the head; real function fec_probe 4391-4671, read in full. Old rejections were mechanical ('name not in slice'), right.

name: fs_enet_start_xmit
prose: ndo_start_xmit for the Freescale fs_enet driver (fs_enet-main.c:452-581; slice cut the head). With CONFIG_FS_ENET_MPC5121_FEC, if skb->data or any fragment offset is not 4-byte aligned it calls tx_skb_align_workaround, which linearizes skb in place (skb_linearize, which modifies the original), allocates a new skb, copies the data and frees the original skb with dev_kfree_skb_any, returning the new skb; if linearize or the allocation fails it returns NULL and fs_enet_start_xmit returns NETDEV_TX_BUSY with the original skb not freed (but possibly already linearized). After a successful workaround the local skb is the copy and the original has been freed. It then takes fep->tx_lock; if fep->tx_free <= nr_frags or the current descriptor still has BD_ENET_TX_READY set, it stops the queue, drops the lock, logs 'tx queue full!' and returns NETDEV_TX_BUSY; in that case, when the workaround had replaced the skb, the original skb the stack will retry has already been freed and the copy is not freed or returned to the caller. Otherwise it adds skb->len to tx_bytes, decrements tx_free by nr_frags + 1, maps the linear part and each fragment into consecutive descriptors (marking fragment slots as mapped-as-page and not owning an skb), sets the ready/last/interrupt flags (with pad when skb->len <= 60), stores skb in the last descriptor's tx_skbuff slot, advances cur_tx, stops the queue if tx_free < MAX_SKB_FRAGS, timestamps, calls tx_kickstart, unlocks and returns NETDEV_TX_OK. It does not check dma_mapping_error on the mappings.
note: Reviewers: original (workaround frees original; ring full then BUSY does not retain it), round-2 (same, caller not updated) and round-15 (after successful linearize, original is modified when alloc fails) are all right: 476-483, 424-448, 493-501. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head.

name: gfar_start_xmit
prose: ndo_start_xmit for the Freescale gianfar (eTSEC) driver (gianfar.c:1758-1998; slice cut the head). The caller does not need to hold the Tx queue lock for this function's own bookkeeping: it takes tx_queue->txlock itself, with spin_lock_bh, only around the update of num_txbdfree (1960-1963). The queue is chosen by skb->queue_mapping. If a frame control block is needed (checksum/VLAN, or timestamp which also needs TxPAL) it calls skb_cow_head; failure counts a tx_error, frees the skb with dev_kfree_skb_any and returns NETDEV_TX_OK (1796). It computes the descriptors needed (nr_frags + 1, or + 2 for a hardware timestamp); if that exceeds tx_queue->num_txbdfree it stops the queue, increments tx_fifo_errors and returns NETDEV_TX_BUSY without consuming the skb (1814). Otherwise it adds the byte and packet counts to the queue stats (before any mapping can fail), prepares the FCB/TxPAL, optionally falls back to skb_checksum_help for checksum errata cases, maps the linear part and each fragment, fills the descriptors, sets the first descriptor's status last (after gfar_wmb), records the skb in tx_skbuff, advances skb_curtx and cur_tx, decrements num_txbdfree under txlock, stops the queue if no descriptors remain, writes TSTAT to un-halt the DMA and returns NETDEV_TX_OK (1977). If any DMA mapping fails (the linear part or a fragment) it goes to dma_map_err, which clears TXBD_READY and unmaps the fragment descriptors that were already set up (the loop starts at the descriptor after the first one, so the linear-part mapping at 1861 is not unmapped there), frees the skb and returns NETDEV_TX_OK; the stats counted earlier are not reverted.
note: Reviewer (precondition says caller holds the Tx queue lock but function acquires tx_queue->txlock itself) is right: 1960-1963. Additional findings: linear-part mapping not unmapped on a later fragment mapping failure; stats not rolled back. Slice cut the head; real function 1758-1998.
